chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ismail ibn Marar, from Yunus, from Mansur ibn Hazim, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him)

Regarding a man who died and left a slave, so one of his children testified that his father had emancipated him. He (peace be upon him) said: 'His testimony is accepted, and he is not liable for compensation, and the slave is made to work (serve) for what belonged to the other inheritors.'

key_terms.لَا يُغْرَمُ: He is not liable for compensation
key_terms.يُسْتَسْعَى: He is made to work/serve (to compensate)

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling if one heir claims the deceased freed a slave?
ai.summary: This ruling from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) establishes the principle of 'istis'a' (compensation through service) in Shia jurisprudence, balancing the validity of a single heir's testimony for emancipation with the financial rights of the remaining co-heirs. It highlights the practical application of debt settlement within inheritance law, where the freed slave's labor offsets the value deducted from the claiming heir's share, ensuring equity among all beneficiaries.
